intent: Authenticated cardholder asks for the £600 hotel entry to be returned to available balance today, believing the hotel charged £1,120 for a £520 stay.
summary: Ledger shows one booked debit of £520 (FINAL-022); the £600 is an active authorisation reservation (AUTH-022) linked to it, reducing available (£380) not ledger (£980) balance. Hotel receipt confirms final £520 under the same references. Decision: request card operations to investigate AUTH-022 and release it if eligible under the E04 procedure, marked time-sensitive; then reply to the customer explaining hold vs. debit, that the request is raised, that the desk cannot release it and same-day timing cannot be promised.

facts.claim: Account holder Rois Fenwick; current contact authentication recorded as passed; chat channel is authenticated.
Only one card debit is booked: FINAL-022, -£520.00, linked to AUTH-022, booked 2026-11-10T08:30.
AUTH-022 is an authorisation_reservation of £600.00 with status 'active' at 2026-11-10T09:00; it is not a booked debit.
Ledger balance snapshot £980.00 (1,500 − 520); available balance snapshot £380.00 (980 − 600 reservation).
Hotel final receipt SYN-HOTEL-022 states final amount paid by card £520.00, payment reference FINAL-022, authorisation reference AUTH-022; stay ended 2026-11-10.

Card operations can investigate a lingering linked authorisation after a completed purchase and release an eligible stale hold after checking linkage and current network state; case desk may request investigation but cannot release a hold; release timing depends on those checks.
Customer asks for the £600 to be returned to available funds today and states they need groceries.

missing: Current card-network state of AUTH-022 (whether the merchant has released or will release the authorisation) — only card operations can check this
Card operations' eligibility determination and release timing for AUTH-022

steps.instruction: Request card operations to investigate the lingering linked authorisation on account SYN-ACCT-B022: AUTH-022, £600.00, status active, recorded 2026-11-10T09:00, linked to booked card debit FINAL-022 (−£520.00, 2026-11-10T08:30). Pass: merchant Alderclock Hotel receipt SYN-HOTEL-022 (issued 2026-11-10 09:10) confirming final amount £520.00 with payment reference FINAL-022 and authorisation reference AUTH-022, stay ended 2026-11-10. Ask them to check linkage and current network state and release the hold if eligible under the card servicing procedure; mark as time-sensitive because the customer states they need the funds today for groceries; ask them to confirm the outcome and expected timing back to the case desk.

rationale.explanation: The ledger and merchant receipt both show one completed purchase of £520 with a still-active £600 authorisation under the same reference, matching the E04 procedure's 'lingering linked authorisation following a completed purchase'. The desk cannot release it, so the only supported route is a card operations investigation request.
rationale.criterion: Case desk may request card operations investigation of a lingering linked authorisation; only card operations can release an eligible stale hold after linkage and network-state checks.

steps.instruction: Reply: 'I've checked your account. Only £520 has actually been taken — that is the hotel's final charge (reference FINAL-022, booked 08:30 today), and your ledger balance is £980. The £600 you see is not a second charge: it is the authorisation hold the hotel placed when you checked in, which is still showing as active and is linked to the same stay. The hotel has not taken £1,120. While the hold stays active it reduces your available balance to £380. I have raised a request with our card operations team to check this hold against the completed £520 payment and release it if it qualifies, and I have marked it as urgent because you need the money today. I have to be honest that our desk cannot release the hold directly and the timing depends on card operations' checks, so I can't guarantee it will be back today. I will update you as soon as they respond. If the delay is leaving you struggling to cover essentials, our financial support team can help — let me know if you'd like that.' If the s1 request has not been acknowledged as sent, state that the request is being raised rather than that it has been raised.

rationale.explanation: The customer's misunderstanding (£1,120 taken) is answered directly by the supplied ledger and receipt; the reply must state only the proven stage (debit booked, authorisation active) and that release is pending with card operations, without promising a same-day outcome.
rationale.criterion: Distinguish authorisation from debit and state only the stage the record proves; a release request is not a completed release; do not promise timing absent an applicable commitment.

must_state: Only £520 has actually been taken from the account (FINAL-022, booked 08:30); the ledger balance is £980
The £600 (AUTH-022) is an active authorisation hold linked to that purchase, not a second charge; the hotel has not taken £1,120
The hold reduces available balance (£380) until it is released
A request to card operations to investigate and release the hold if eligible has been raised (pending execution acknowledgement) and marked time-sensitive
The case desk cannot release the hold itself; release timing depends on card operations' linkage and network checks, so same-day release cannot be guaranteed
The customer will be updated once card operations respond; if the delay causes hardship, the bank's financial support team can be contacted
must_not: Do not say the hotel charged twice or that £1,120 was debited
Do not promise the £600 will be available today or at any specific time
Do not claim the hold has been released or that card operations have acted
Do not ask for PIN, password or one-time code
Do not speculate about a merchant error or fraud cause for the lingering hold
